<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919374_theRebbe_640" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919374_theRebbe_640__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Opening header with date and reference.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven*.</t>
    <t s="1">Fifteen Tammuz,</t>
    <t s="2">the year 5742*</t>
    <t s="3">*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Learning Torah in a group draws a higher revelation of the thirteen attributes of mercy, beyond the measure of the arousal from below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Ten who sit and engage in Torah, the Divine Presence dwells among them"1,</t>
    <t s="1">and it is explained by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe of the Geulah, in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh" that was given for the first celebration of Yud-Beis Tammuz</t>
    <t s="2">(the year 5688),</t>
    <t s="3">that even one who sits and engages in Torah draws down a revelation of G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="4">as the continuation of the Mishnah states: "And from where [do we derive] even five... even three... even two... even one...",</t>
    <t s="5">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="6">the drawing down through the Torah of many is a more elevated drawing down.</t>
    <t s="7">For just as regarding prayer, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said2</t>
    <t s="8">"The prayer of the many is not rejected,"</t>
    <t s="9">because through the prayer of the many, the thirteen attributes of mercy that are above the chain of descent are drawn down,</t>
    <t s="10">and moreover3</t>
    <t s="11">the drawing down from above through the prayer of the many is not commensurate with the measure of their arousal from below</t>
    <t s="12">(even not commensurate with the measure of the arousal from below of the many),</t>
    <t s="13">so too is it regarding Torah,</t>
    <t s="14">that through the study of Torah by the many, there is a drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy that are above the chain of descent</t>
    <t s="15">[For although the drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy through the engagement in Torah is due to the virtue of Torah,</t>
    <t s="16">that the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded correspond to the thirteen attributes of mercy,</t>
    <t s="17">from this it is understood</t>
    <t s="18">that the drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy also occurs when one sits and engages in Torah,</t>
    <t s="19">nevertheless, the drawing down of the thirteen attributes of mercy through engagement in Torah is primarily through Torah study specifically in public,</t>
    <t s="20">meaning that the level of the thirteen attributes of mercy that is drawn down through engagement in Torah in public is a more elevated level],</t>
    <t s="21">and moreover,</t>
    <t s="22">the drawing down through the study of Torah by the many is not commensurate with the measure of the study of the many.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The connection between Torah and prayer is hinted at in the Mishnah's verse about the Temple, where the Divine Presence dwells through both.</sectionSummarySection>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that the analogy of Torah to prayer</t>
    <t s="3">is also hinted at in the aforementioned Mishnah: "And from where [do we derive] even one? As it is stated4</t>
    <t s="4">'In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you,'"</t>
    <t s="5">"In every place" etc. refers to the Holy Temple</t>
    <t s="6">[a place where the Divine Presence comes,</t>
    <t s="7">"I will come to you"],</t>
    <t s="8">where permission was given to pronounce the explicit name</t>
    <t s="9">["I cause My name to be mentioned"]5,</t>
    <t s="10">and the Holy Temple is related to the pillar of service,</t>
    <t s="11">sacrifices6</t>
    <t s="12">and prayer7</t>
    <t s="13">[And to add,</t>
    <t s="14">that even the Priestly Blessing, in which they would mention the Name as it is written in the Holy Temple5,</t>
    <t s="15">was after the offering of the daily morning sacrifice8</t>
    <t s="16">(the beginning of all the sacrifices),</t>
    <t s="17">and also nowadays the Sages instituted the Priestly Blessing in prayer9,</t>
    <t s="18">and within the prayer itself – in the blessing of the service10].</t>
    <t s="19">And in the Mishnah, this verse is brought</t>
    <t s="20">("In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you")</t>
    <t s="21">regarding the indwelling of the Divine Presence through the study of Torah,</t>
    <t s="22">and from this it is implied that Torah and prayer are related to each other, and specifically in this matter.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
